summary: Self-contained offline browser page (index.html, inline JS port of transform.py, no dependencies, CSP connect-src none) reproduces the synthetic example byte-for-byte and matches transform.py on 20 differential cases; its UI scripts pass 11/11 checks under a Node vm DOM stub. It has NOT been executed in a real browser: no browser is installed in the sandbox.

differential.compared: ok, counts, exact error and warning text, output file names and output bytes vs python3 transform.py
cases_include: 9000 barcodes split at 5000 (JS 400 ms in Node)

dom_stub.note: Runs actual inline scripts with stubbed document/FileReader/Blob/URL; first run 10/11 failed because the test input 120,00 splits into two CSV fields (test fixture defect, corrected to 12.345, code unchanged).

not_verified: execution in any real browser (rendering, file picker, FileReader encoding, Blob download naming)
memory/speed in browsers for very large files
non-ASCII digit and astral-character sort edge cases (Python and JS can differ; not tested)
not_done: no deployment, no site change, no outreach, no price, no demand or revenue claim
next_step_if_continued: Someone with a real browser (founder or reviewer) opens index.html locally, loads the two fixture CSVs, and confirms the downloaded file equals fixtures/after-shopify.csv; only then propose adding it to site shopify-catalogue-example via exact-digest independent review.
